body.heading: Lie back and look up
paragraphs: On a day with puffy white clouds, lie on a blanket outside with your adult and look up. Let your eyes relax.
Clouds are made of tiny drops of water floating in the air. Up close they would feel like fog. From down here, they look like floating islands.

body.heading: Spot the shapes
paragraphs: Call out what you can see in the clouds: a dragon, a ship, a giant's face, a sleeping cat. There are no wrong shapes.
Watch one cloud for a while. It changes as it drifts, growing new parts and losing old ones. Your dragon might slowly turn into a boat.

body.heading: Tell the cloud's story
paragraphs: Pick your favourite cloud and tell its story together. Where is it going? Who lives on it? What happens when it rains?
Swap storytellers halfway through and let the story change direction. Cloud stories are allowed to be as drifting as clouds.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: lie back, spot shapes in the clouds, and tell stories about them.

safetyNotes: Never look directly at the Sun while cloud watching; if the Sun is near your cloud, move your blanket or look at a different cloud.
Lie down somewhere safe with your adult, away from roads, and come inside if the weather turns stormy.
screenFreeExtension: Draw the best cloud shape you saw and write its story underneath before you forget it.
takeaway: Clouds are free pictures in the sky, and they change while you watch.
